why: A bookstore sells books by ISBN, tracks second-hand stock and manages customer wishes. Distinct from the library circulation model: this is a sales model, not a lending model.
operator: The bookstore owner manages inventory, purchases from suppliers and customer wish lists. Their day is receiving shipments, pricing copies and matching customers to books they want.
entities: Bookstore (id, nameAr, nameEn, branchId, address, phone, currency, taxRegistration, openingHours)
Product (id, bookstoreId, sku, isbn, titleAr, titleEn, authorAr, authorEn, category, unitPricePiasters, costPiasters, taxRate, condition, status, locationShelf)
Customer (id, bookstoreId, name, phone, whatsAppOptIn, purchaseHistoryCount, totalSpentPiasters)
Wishlist (id, customerId, productId, notes, createdAt, notified)
PurchaseOrder (id, supplierId, status, lines, expectedAt, totalPiasters)
Staff (id, bookstoreId, name, phone, role, hourlyRatePiasters, status)
batches: No : bookstore carries no stock or expiry (condition indicates wear, not expiry)
expiry: Not applicable. Books have condition states not expiry dates
special: The core structures are the product catalogue with condition states, the wishlist system and the customer purchase history. Condition (new/used) replaces expiry for second-hand stock.
screens: Product catalogue: grid of books with title, author, ISBN, price, condition (new/used), availability
Product detail: full book info, edition notes, condition description, purchase options
Wishlist manager: customer wishes, notify when available, prioritise purchases
Customer profile: purchase history, total spent, wishlist, opt-in status
Purchase order: receive shipment from supplier, record items, update stock
Cash register: scan SKU, apply discount, tender payment, print receipt
Staff shift: clock in/out, customer load per hour, notes
roles: Owner: everything : inventory, pricing, reports, billing
Cashier: scan items, apply discounts, tender payment, print receipt
Stock clerk: receive shipments, update stock, relocate products
Assistant: customer wishlist management, special orders
reports: Sales by day and hour: revenue per period, peak hours
Product popularity: most sold books, editions, authors per period
Customer lifetime value: total spent, visit frequency, average ticket
Wishlist conversion: how many wishes turned into purchases
Inventory aging: how long copies have been in stock by condition
integrations: Barcode scanner for SKU entry at till
Esc/POS thermal printer for receipts and special orders
WhatsApp deep link for customer notifications (new arrivals, wished-back-in-stock)
Email for invoice and special order updates (opt-in)
onboarding: Shop basics: name, branch, address, phone, currency, working hours
Initial inventory: the starting book list with ISBN, titles, prices and condition
Product categories: fiction, non-fiction, children, academic, second-hand
Staff: add the initial team with their role templates
First week plan: receive first shipment, list first products, first customer sale
seed: No sector-specific seed data. The engine provides the product catalogue with condition states and role templates.

tasks.title: Add product catalogue grid with condition states
tasks.brief: Build the product catalogue: grid of books with title, author, ISBN, price, condition (new/used), availability. Done when the catalogue loads and displays books from Firestore with correct condition badges.
tasks.done: When product catalogue displays live data with condition badges

tasks.title: Add wishlist manager per customer
tasks.brief: Build the wishlist screen: customer wishes, notify when available, prioritise purchases. Done when a wishlist item can be added and the notification flag is saved.
tasks.done: When wishlist manager works and saves notification flag

tasks.title: Add customer profile with purchase history
tasks.brief: Build the customer profile screen: purchase history, total spent, wishlist, opt-in status. Done when the profile saves and displays customer data correctly.
tasks.done: When customer profile works and displays live data

tasks.title: Add purchase order receipt screen
tasks.brief: Build the purchase order screen: receive shipment from supplier, record items, update stock. Done when the order saves and stock increments correctly.
tasks.done: When purchase order works end-to-end and stock updates

tasks.title: Add cash register with SKU scanning
tasks.brief: Build the cash register: scan SKU, apply discount, tender payment, print receipt. Done when the sale is recorded and receipt prints correctly.
tasks.done: When cash register works end-to-end and receipt prints

tasks.title: Add customer lifetime value report
tasks.brief: Build the LTV report: total spent, visit frequency, average ticket per customer. Done when the report computes from Firestore and displays correct figures.
tasks.done: When LTV report pulls live data and displays correctly

tasks.title: Add wishlist conversion report
tasks.brief: Build the report showing how many wishes turned into purchases per period. Done when the report computes from Firestore and displays correct conversion rates.
tasks.done: When wishlist conversion report computes correctly from live data

tasks.title: Add inventory aging report by condition
tasks.brief: Build the aging report: copies in stock by condition (new/used) and how long. Done when the report computes from Firestore and displays correct aging buckets.
tasks.done: When inventory aging report computes correctly from live data

tasks.title: Add onboarding flow for initial bookstore setup
tasks.brief: Build the onboarding flow: shop basics, initial inventory, product categories, staff addition. Done when the flow completes and the shop appears with all defaults.
tasks.done: When onboarding flow works end-to-end and shop is created

tasks.title: Add personalisation engraving flow
tasks.brief: Build the engraving flow: enter text, real-time preview on product item, save engraving details per order. Done when the engraving text is saved and preview updates instantly.
tasks.done: When personalisation engraving flow works end-to-end

risks: No special-category data risks (this is a retail sales model)
Encryption key loss makes product records unrecoverable
WhatsApp template rejection if not approved by Meta
Second-hand condition descriptions must not mislead buyers consumer-protection law
